_comment: Empirical calibration of Composite Score -> actual historical hit rate, fit from the 733 graded Recommendations rows in the live Notion 'Recommendations' database, 2026-06-17 to 2026-07-31. This is the answer to 'can we use ML/prediction models': a full predictive model on ~730 rows across 45 days would overfit badly, but a simple empirical calibration table is exactly the right amount of model for this much data, and it is honest about where it's thin. Refresh quarterly via calibration.refit_from_records() as more graded data accumulates — see src/analysis/calibration.py.

buckets.note: n=5 — too small to trust on its own; 1 of 5 rows (HDFCBANK 2026-07-14) is a known stale-ref-price data bug, not a real -55.8% move. Treat this band as UNCALIBRATED until re-fit on clean data; do not size up on a raw 'Strong Buy' label yet.
Below coin-flip and net-negative average move despite being the 2nd-highest score band — do not scale position size up in this band until re-fit.
Best-calibrated, highest-volume band — the composite score genuinely works here.
Near coin-flip for the 'Avoid/Sell' band, and the average move was POSITIVE — stocks flagged Avoid/Sell did not, on average, actually decline. Weakest band besides Strong Buy.
